result.summary: Replaces memcpy with std::copy in CHMAC_SHA256 and CHMAC_SHA512 so that zero-length HMAC keys do not pass a null pointer to memcpy and trigger UBSan warnings. It adds empty-key test vectors to crypto_tests and removes empty-input workarounds from the crypto and eval_script fuzz targets.
result.problem: Calling memcpy with a null pointer even for zero bytes is undefined behavior in C++, triggering UBSan runtime warnings and forcing fuzz targets to add defensive checks against empty byte vectors.

result.card: This PR replaces memcpy with std::copy in CHMAC_SHA256 and CHMAC_SHA512 to avoid undefined behavior and UBSan null-pointer warnings when initializing HMAC with empty keys. It adds empty-key HMAC test vectors and removes unnecessary empty-input guards in the crypto and eval_script fuzz targets. The change improves the correctness of cryptographic primitives under sanitizers and enables cleaner fuzz coverage of edge cases. The code has an approval from sedited after addressing suggestions from maflcko, though the author has been inactive for over 60 days.
